MVW 11.1, 22.9 and 22.10 match the objects. Perfectness is not imposed; the proof handles finite fields through transfers; the semilocal running convention uses arbitrary finite point sets.

Finite prime avoidance identifies the maximal ideals with inclusion-maximal selected primes. Removing redundant generalizations preserves the neighborhood system. The induction uses points closed in S, not necessarily in X.
Quasi-projectivity gives common affine neighborhoods cofinal inside every ambient open neighborhood, matching the standard essentially smooth extension.
G2 supplies transfers on the separated reflection. G1 and generic injectivity show F(S)->sF(S) injective; quotient maps and filtered colimits give surjectivity. Sheafification stays unchanged.

Separatedness gives injection into the sheafification on the overlap after filtered colimits without assuming the overlap semilocal. Empty overlaps and disconnected components are covered by additivity and the empty-scheme sheaf axiom.

V excludes the first closed point, forcing every successful G3 shrink U to retain that point while continuing to exclude the other closed points. Exact refinements stay in the same filtered cofinal system.

The localizations and their fiber-product overlap are represented by the stated neighborhood and intersection limits. Filtered-colimit exactness applies without a coherent global choice of refinements.
The sheaf row is only left exact. The supplied element chase uses middle isomorphism and right injection to prove left surjectivity; left injectivity already comes from separatedness.
The single-closed-point base case is equality of stalks. This proves the full arbitrary-field and finite-point-set target.
The multiplication-by-two illustration is correct and is not presented as a counterexample to the original geometric lemma.
